content:
oliver: Saw a sharp increase in OOMs on prod after merge 9f7a3b this morning. Several hosts in cluster-prod-3 crashed with OOM kills.

oliver: Quick perf summary:
```
perf top:
  45.2% kv_hash_insert
  18.1% slab_alloc
   8.6% memcpy
kv_stats: live_slabs=32768, free_slabs=120, alloc_rate=220k/s, avg_obj=48B
```

sophie: I re-ran the traffic replay and the sequence-length distribution shifted right -> many more short requests (<= 64 tokens). That increases churn in the small-object path.

kevin: did a git bisect, blame narrowed to commit a1b2c3d4 (hash-randomize/stripe-mapping). The change replaced per-core mixing with a global seed.

kevin: bisect log:
```
> git bisect start
> good 8e3f2... v9.2.1
> bad 9f7a3b... release/9f8
> first bad commit a1b2c3d4
```

maria: CI perf job `kv_mem_pressure_longctx` failed on master: +28% resident mem vs baseline. Link: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/3721

oliver: hypothesis: global seed reduces hash entropy per-core causing higher collision rates and hot slab chains -> lock contention and cache-inefficient allocations. With short seqs we recycle same keys and hit the same slab pages.

sophie: quick repro locally with `tools/kv_stress --clients 2k --seq-dist short.json` shows identical perf spike. Repro script:
```
RUST_LOG=info ./bin/run_kv_stress -c 2000 -s short_seq_dist.json
```

kevin: opened PR to revert the hash change (PR #3721). Small, single-line revert of the seeding change. https://git.redwood/example/pr/3721

infra-bot: Canary rollback initiated on cluster-prod-3 by @kevin — rollback tag v9.8.0-canary -> v9.7.4

ci-bot: Alert: perf/regression checks failing for release/9f8 — gating on memory-alloc-rate, failing threshold 15% (observed 28%).

maria: I'll run heap profiles across the canary hosts and dump sample slab chains.

oliver: temporary mitigation: enable per-core prefetcher and reduce small-slab growth threshold. I pushed a config change to prod-config: `kv.small_slab_growth=0.5` (rollout in progress).

sophie: ack — running extended verify. If revert PR lands we should re-run full perf suite before rolling forward.

oliver: monitoring dashboards now. Will post heap profiles in this thread when available. Thanks everyone :pray:
